clue.text: Managers with gold, possibly, in grand accommodation

parts.note: a board of directors manages a company
and means with, joining things

indicators.note: possibly says these letters might be arranged some other way

parts.note: taken as written
G is short for grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: Company managers, perhaps paid in gold, live in grand lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges GOLD into LODG, which with IN and G (grand) makes the third word.
explanation.definitionFit: Room plus meals provided for a lodger is a standard form of accommodation.

clue.text: Singer touring Jolson's place in New York state

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the singer's letters surround the other piece

parts.note: a buffo is a comic bass singer in opera
Al Jolson was the American singer of The Jazz Singer

explanation.surface: A singer on tour visits a venue associated with Al Jolson upstate.
explanation.definitionFit: Buffalo is a large city in the north-west of New York state.

clue.text: A charming kind of accent

parts.note: cute means charming, delightfully attractive

explanation.surface: Someone has a delightfully appealing way of speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: The acute is a diacritic mark, as in café, a type of accent written over a letter.

clue.text: Putting up duty list, registered a small charge

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting up means the letters are read from bottom to top, so the whole run is turned round

parts.note: a rota is a list of duties and who does them
noted means registered, taken note of

explanation.surface: An office posts a staff rota and records a modest fee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Putting up' turns the whole run ROTANOTED backwards, giving DETON then ATOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A detonator is a small explosive charge used to set off a larger one.

clue.text: He gives the game away? Bother

definitions.meaning: an informer who betrays secrets to the police, a copper's snitch
to annoy or irritate, in British slang

explanation.definitionFit: In British slang the word is both a police informer and a verb meaning to irritate.

clue.text: Fat pig for reception, once left at sea

indicators.note: the fat is there to receive the pig, so one piece is held within the other

parts.note: lard is pig fat used in cooking
a boar is a male pig

explanation.surface: Pork fat is served up to accompany a pig at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Larboard is the old nautical word for the port, left-hand, side of a ship.

clue.text: Dirty-looking tailless old dog

indicators.note: tailless says the word loses its last letter

parts.note: dingy means drab and dirty-looking

explanation.surface: A scruffy aged dog has lost its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: The dingo is the wild dog of Australia.

clue.text: Metalworker working this morning, no good being left out

indicators.note: working means the letters are put to work in a new order
being left out says some letters of the pool are dropped from the result

explanation.surface: A smith is at work this morning, but someone useless has been dropped from the shift.
explanation.walkthrough: Take NG out of THISMORNING and rearrange the remaining nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An ironsmith is a craftsman who forges iron, a type of metalworker.

clue.text: Elderly prisoner serving bird?

parts.note: grey describes the hair of the elderly, so grey means old
a lag is a convict serving time, as in old lag

explanation.surface: An aged convict is doing time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bird' in British slang also means a prison sentence, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The greylag is a grey wild goose, the ancestor of most farmyard geese.

clue.text: Gooseberries may accompany one's dates in the stalls

definitions.text: Gooseberries may accompany one's dates in the stalls

parts.words: Gooseberries may accompany one's dates in the stalls
parts.note: read as a gooseberry tagging along with a courting couple at the theatre, but really a trader whose market stall sells both kinds of fruit

explanation.definitionFit: A seller of fruit at a market stall would stock gooseberries alongside dates.

clue.text: She wept at home over an award

indicators.note: over says the word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: in means at home
the OBE, Order of the British Empire, is a British honour

explanation.surface: A woman cried when back home with her honour.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Niobe wept endlessly for her slain children and was turned into a weeping rock.

clue.text: Declining a drink? He finally accepted gallons

indicators.note: the drink accepted, or took in, the letter

parts.note: gin is a drink

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone turns down a drink, but he eventually agrees to gallons of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepted' puts E (He finally) inside GIN, making GEIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Ageing means growing old, declining in strength with years.

clue.text: Massive failure in fossil fuel

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: coal is a fossil fuel
a loss is a failure, a defeat

explanation.surface: A huge disaster has hit the coal industry.
explanation.definitionFit: Colossal is a synonym of huge, enormous in size.

clue.text: Decorated old sailors at end of battle

parts.note: RN, the Royal Navy, stands for sailors

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Veteran seamen received medals after the fighting ended.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornate means elaborately adorned with ornament.

clue.text: Reporter has fresh probe round hospital

parts.note: new means fresh

indicators.note: the probe goes round the other letter, holding it inside

parts.note: a sound is a surgeon's probe; to sound is to probe
H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A journalist carries out a new investigation around a hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: A newshound is an informal word for a keen journalist hunting stories.

clue.text: He missed the English spring, getting a tan

definitions.meaning: the Victorian poet who wrote Home Thoughts from Abroad, longing for an English April from Italy

explanation.definitionFit: Robert Browning wrote 'Oh, to be in England now that April's there'; browning also means tanning.

clue.text: Enlightened, to take addictive drug? Check to That's a joke!

parts.note: wise means enlightened, knowing
crack is a highly addictive form of cocaine

explanation.surface: Someone claims taking drugs brings enlightenment, which is laughable.
explanation.definitionFit: A wisecrack is a witty remark, a quip.

clue.text: Both came adrift, making great sacrifice

indicators.note: adrift means loose and wandering, so the letters drift out of order

explanation.surface: Two boats broke loose, a costly loss.
explanation.definitionFit: A hecatomb was originally an ancient sacrifice of a hundred oxen, hence any great slaughter.

clue.text: Recompensed draughtsman returning keys

indicators.note: returning means the word is read backwards

parts.note: a drawer is one who draws, a draughtsman
E and D are musical keys

explanation.surface: A designer is paid back for handing in the keys.
explanation.definitionFit: Rewarded means paid or recompensed for something done.

clue.text: Audibly regret gibe — it's indistinct on stage

indicators.note: audibly means the word is heard, so its spoken form gives different letters

parts.note: rue means regret
a barb is a cutting gibe

explanation.surface: Someone is sorry for a mocking comment muttered in a play.
explanation.definitionFit: Actors murmuring 'rhubarb' produce indistinct background crowd noise on stage.

clue.text: Home of islander, one attending school — in Iowa

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
IA is the postal abbreviation for Iowa

explanation.surface: An islander's son goes to school in the American Midwest.
explanation.definitionFit: Ischia is an island in the Bay of Naples, so it is where an islander lives.

clue.text: Female composer, say, one involved in breakdown

indicators.note: say signals that the words are spoken, giving letters that sound the same

parts.note: the girl's name Anna followed by the composer Liszt

explanation.surface: A woman composer is one of those taking part in a nervous collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' gives a word sounding like Anna Liszt.
explanation.definitionFit: An analyst breaks a thing down into its parts, so is involved in breakdown, its analysis.

clue.text: At university, books are taken in to cure disorder

parts.note: up means at university, in residence

indicators.note: taken in says the books go inside the other word

parts.note: heal means cure
AV, the Authorized Version, is a set of biblical books

explanation.surface: University students take in books in an effort to remedy chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: An upheaval is a violent disturbance, a disruption.

clue.text: It's mostly serving as a protein

indicators.note: mostly says the word loses its last letter

parts.note: acting means serving as, standing in

explanation.surface: Something is largely being used as a protein.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' removes the last G of ACTING.
explanation.definitionFit: Actin is a muscle protein that works with myosin in contraction.

clue.text: Tropical shrub two aircraftmen observed way back

parts.note: AC stands for aircraftman
the second of the two aircraftmen

indicators.note: back means the road's name is read backwards

parts.note: the A1, Britain's Great North Road, written with I for the figure one

explanation.surface: Two RAF men spotted a tropical bush far back along the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses AI to IA; 'observed' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: Acacias are tropical and subtropical trees and shrubs such as wattle.

clue.text: Frederick's daughter's introduction to Charles Lamb

indicators.note: introduction to picks the first letter of the word

parts.note: Elia was the pen name of the essayist Charles Lamb

explanation.surface: A duke's daughter is presented to the essayist Charles Lamb.
explanation.definitionFit: In As You Like It, Celia is the daughter of the usurping Duke Frederick.

clue.text: Tool mad zealot can provide

indicators.note: the words can provide the letters strung along within them

explanation.surface: A fanatic might be able to supply an axe-like tool.
explanation.definitionFit: An adze is a woodworking tool with an arched blade at right angles to the handle.

clue.text: A mostly dreary time for a mature person

indicators.note: mostly says the word loses its last letter

parts.note: dull means dreary

explanation.surface: Middle age is a largely boring period for a grown-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts the final L from DULL.
explanation.definitionFit: An adult is a fully grown, mature person.

clue.text: Trouble in former Turkish governor's court

parts.note: old means former

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: a bey was a governor in the Ottoman Empire
ail means trouble, as in what ails you

explanation.surface: There was unrest in an ex-Ottoman official's tribunal.
explanation.walkthrough: The OLD BAILEY is London's Central Criminal Court.
explanation.definitionFit: The Old Bailey is the familiar name of the Central Criminal Court in London.

clue.text: Boy in group quickly goes to rest in accommodation (3,3,9) 23,297 Solution

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: a band is a group of musicians
Ed is a boy's name
a break is a rest
fast means quickly

explanation.surface: A lad in a band hurries to bed at his lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes to' just links FAST to BREAK.
explanation.definitionFit: A guest house offering a bed and morning meal is a form of accommodation.
